title: Admin Pathway Mapper — Consolidated Access & Audit Journey (compact prototype)
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Admins and security reviewers struggle to answer cross-cutting questions quickly: who had a given permission at time T, what actions led to a role change, and what downstream resources were affected? The current console surfaces roles, workspace settings, and audit events in separate places which increases cognitive load and support tickets.

Goal: Ship a compact, scannable prototype that consolidates role/permission state, a time-based change playback, and correlated audit events into an "Admin Pathway Mapper" view. This should accelerate access reviews, reduce support escalations, and enable faster incident triage.

Scope: Design a single-row compact timeline per principal (user/service account/role) that shows granted/removed permissions, approvals, and related API events (deploys, model-rollouts, console logins). Include quick actions: snapshot-to-policy, open-permission-simulator, and export-audit. Deliverables: Figma prototype (desktop/tablet), clickable playback micro-interaction, annotated accessibility and copy guidelines, and a 6-user usability test plan.

Out of scope: Full policy engine changes, backend schemas. We'll consume an API contract provided by ENG-84219 (audit-correlation-index).
acceptance_criteria: Clickable Figma prototype showing: (a) compact timeline rows for at least three principal types, (b) hover tooltip with event metadata, (c) snapshot-to-policy flow, (d) quick export to CSV/JSON
Annotated handoff spec with tokens, spacing, states and ARIA guidance
Usability test completed with 6 participants (mix of admin, security, and platform engineer) and a short report summarizing top 3 usability issues and suggested fixes
Design review approval from PM (Riley Chen) and Security (Leah Okafor)
List of front-end acceptance tickets created for Console team (at least 4 tickets) and linked to ENG-84219 dependency
notes:
Key trade-offs discussed: compact vs expanded rows (we chose compact with optional expansion to keep scanability), event density heuristics (sample + cluster similar events to avoid visual noise), and permission semantics (we show effective permissions snapshot; full policy derivations will be a follow-up). We also agreed on a fallback for long timelines: time-window selector + sampling.

Accessibility: provide keyboard-first playback controls, high-contrast event states, and ARIA labels for timeline rows.

Telemetry: track clicks on snapshot-to-policy, export-audit, and playback-start to measure adoption.
